enriched_description: Odonate insect measuring 25-50 mm with slender delicate body smaller than dragonfly. Two pairs of membranous wings with intricate venation; wings folded together over abdomen at rest (distinguishing from dragonfly). Head with large widely separated compound eyes and three ocelli. Antennae short and bristle-like. Thorax narrow and oblique. Abdomen extremely elongate and thread-like comprising 10 segments. Integument iridescent in blue, green, red, or metallic tones. Legs slender and weak adapted for perching rather than grasping. Inherited arthropod traits include chitinous exoskeleton, segmented body with three tagmata, and six jointed legs. Non-stinging with aquatic nymphal stage.

Nymphalid butterfly with wingspan 50-75 mm. Wings predominantly black or dark brown with striking white bands and orange-red patches on forewings and hindwings. Body robust and densely hairy. Antennae clubbed with distinct terminal swelling. Legs reduced with forelegs brush-like and non-functional for walking. Wings display bright iridescent coloration with white spots along margins. Ventral wing surface cryptically patterned in brown and gray. Inherited arthropod traits include chitinous exoskeleton, segmented body plan, and six jointed legs. Larvae feed on nettle plants with spiny caterpillar morphology.

Satyrid butterfly with wingspan 30-50 mm. Wings uniformly brown to dark brown with small eyespots (ocelli) arranged in rows on both forewings and hindwings. Body slender and hairy. Antennae clubbed. Wings held closed at rest revealing cryptic ventral patterning. Forelegs reduced and brush-like characteristic of nymphalids. Integument of body brown matching wing coloration. Inherited arthropod traits include chitinous exoskeleton, segmented body with three tagmata, and six jointed legs. Flight low and fluttering near ground vegetation. Larvae feed on grasses.

Large danaid butterfly with wingspan 85-120 mm. Wings vivid orange with prominent black venation and broad black borders containing two rows of white spots. Body black with white speckling. Antennae clubbed and black. Legs black and reduced with forelegs brush-like. Wing pattern highly conspicuous serving as aposematic warning coloration. Ventral surface lighter orange with similar patterning. Inherited arthropod traits include chitinous exoskeleton, segmented body plan, and six jointed legs. Long-distance migratory species. Larvae feed exclusively on milkweed plants accumulating toxic cardenolides.

Pierid butterfly with wingspan 40-60 mm. Wings predominantly white with black apical spots on forewings; females display additional black spots. Body slender and white-hairy. Antennae clubbed with yellow-orange coloration. Legs pale and reduced with forelegs brush-like. Wings held vertically above body at rest. Ventral surface of hindwings pale yellow-green in summer form. Inherited arthropod traits include chitinous exoskeleton, segmented body with three tagmata, and six jointed legs. Larvae (cabbageworms) are green caterpillars with sparse hairs feeding on brassica crops.

Pierid butterfly with wingspan 35-65 mm. Wings uniformly yellow to orange-yellow in males; females may display white or greenish morphs. Wing margins bordered with darker pigmentation. Body slender and matching wing coloration. Antennae clubbed. Legs reduced with forelegs brush-like characteristic of pierids. Wings held vertically at rest. Ventral surface similar to dorsal but slightly paler. Inherited arthropod traits include chitinous exoskeleton, segmented body plan, and six jointed legs. Flight rapid and direct. Larvae green caterpillars feeding on leguminous plants.

Small lycaenid butterfly with wingspan 15-40 mm. Wings variable in coloration including blue, orange, brown, or gray often with iridescent scales on dorsal surface. Many species exhibit metallic blue or copper sheen. Body slender and small. Antennae ringed with white. Legs reduced with forelegs brush-like. Wings often display eyespots or tails on hindwings. Ventral surface cryptically patterned with complex markings. Inherited arthropod traits include chitinous exoskeleton, segmented body with three tagmata, and six jointed legs. Many species have mutualistic associations with ants. Larvae often slug-shaped.

Echinoderm exhibiting pentaradial symmetry with five arms extending from central disk. Body size ranging 5-40 cm diameter. Aboral (upper) surface textured with calcareous ossicles, spines, and pedicellariae. Coloration variable including orange, red, purple, blue, or brown. Oral (lower) surface bears central mouth and ambulacral grooves containing tube feet arranged in rows along each arm. Tube feet suction-cup tipped for locomotion and prey capture. Endoskeleton of calcareous plates. Inherited echinoderm traits include water vascular system and regenerative capacity. Marine benthic organism.

Echinoderm with globular body enclosed in thin spiny test (shell) measuring 3-10 cm diameter. Test composed of fused calcareous plates forming rigid spherical structure. Body covered with numerous movable spines varying in length from short to elongate depending on species. Spines articulate with tubercles on test surface. Coloration purple, black, green, red, or brown. Oral surface bears Aristotle's lantern (jaw apparatus) with five teeth. Aboral surface contains anus. Tube feet emerge between spine bases. Inherited echinoderm traits include pentaradial symmetry and water vascular system.

Echinoderm with flexible elongated sausage-shaped body measuring 10-30 cm. Body wall leathery and thick containing microscopic calcareous ossicles. Coloration brown, black, red, or green. Oral end surrounded by 10-30 branched tentacles (modified tube feet) used for feeding. Body cylindrical with dorsal-ventral differentiation; dorsal surface bears wart-like papillae. Ventral surface has three rows of tube feet for locomotion. Anus at aboral end. Inherited echinoderm traits include water vascular system and pentaradial symmetry (secondarily modified to bilateral). Free-living mud feeder on sea floor.
